newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sugar harvest gears up for 96-97 campaign.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sugar harvest gears up for 96-97 campaign.

text.p: Two weeks before the official start of Mexico's 96-97 sugar crop, industrialists are busy pouring over figures estimating the size of the harvest and export possibilities.

Most estimates are for little drastic change to the crop which ended the 1995-1996 campaign at 4.377 million tonnes although all indications are that exports will rise quiet sharply next year, sources said.
"High carry over inventories will take exports to between 700,000 and 750,000 tonnes next year," said one mill owner who asked to remain anonymous.

Exports in 1996 are scheduled to end the year at 649,521 tonnes with 579,636 tonnes sent abroad in the first nine months of the year and 69,885 tonnes programmed between October and December, the National Sugar Chamber said.
Those exports are already sharply higher than the estimated 300,000 tonnes exported in 1995.
